tVa_K4kq1us.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Goals and Accountability
tVa_K4kq1us.one_line: Muslims must define the outcomes they are working toward and hold themselves to them, with the Prophet as the model.
tVa_K4kq1us.summary: Closing khutbah of the 'Achieving the Outcomes' series. His argument is that effort alone is not enough: Muslims as individuals, communities and an ummah must know what they are trying to achieve, and he fears the ummah has never defined this. Citing Yunus 10:14 (Allah made you successors to see how you act), he asks whether Muslims would bring peace and prosperity if they were put in charge today, and argues they would not, because they do not know what their deen is meant to deliver. Noting that the khutbah falls on the Prophet's birthday, he says the whole series can be replaced with one instruction: follow Muhammad. He builds the model from Al-Kahf 18:6, where Allah tells the Prophet not to exhaust himself: the Prophet worked until Allah said slow down, and on the Day of Judgment he will prostrate until Allah says enough. Only Allah decides when we have done enough. Through Bosworth Smith, Michael Hart and the hadith of his dua for Aisha, he presents a leader of total simplicity whose legacy was people, not buildings. In the second khutbah he 'sounds the alarm' that the community has no defined goals and proposes five: education, mentorship, outreach, financial centralization through zakat, and advocacy, pointing to 700 days of bombardment in Gaza, and asks those who love the Prophet to stand for the ummah he wept for.

outline.heading: Opening
Trying your best is not enough
outline.gist: Effort alone is not acceptable; it is equally important to know what you are trying to achieve. Jannah is the destination, but there must be a clear path to it.

outline.heading: Lacking the ummah's outcome makes the job harder
outline.gist: He never dared speak about what the ummah should achieve, thinking individual and communal outcomes for Muslims in the West were enough. Going through the series, he came to think the missing clarity for the ummah makes everyone's job harder.

outline.heading: Yunus 10:14: would we do well if we called the shots?
outline.gist: Humans have always needed a clear plan. Allah made earlier peoples successors to see how they would act; if Muslims were put in charge today, would they bring prosperity and peace? He argues no, because they do not know what they are here to bring, and that this is one reason they are not in charge.

outline.heading: Discuss the outcomes in every household
outline.gist: He is sad to say we have not spent enough time contemplating what the deen is meant to achieve. Clarity would give us a better chance, so the question must be discussed in households, small communities and on a larger scale.

outline.heading: Follow Muhammad: Islam is emulating him
outline.gist: Falling unplanned on the day of his birth, the khutbah makes the point that everything he has ever said could be thrown out and replaced with 'be like Muhammad'. Islam has never been more than emulating him, and his life is found in the Quran.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf 18:6: exhausting yourself for them
outline.gist: The verse he opened with, repeated twice in the Quran and in the surah read every Jumuah. 'Bakhi'' means to use something up completely, like stripping land of its minerals; Allah told the Prophet he would harm himself grieving over people who would not listen.

outline.heading: A work ethic Allah had to slow down
outline.gist: He pushed himself in pursuit of his ummah's goals until revelation told him to take it easy. No one will hear that from the sheikh: the rest of us need to push harder.

outline.heading: Judgment Day: the only sujud told 'enough'
outline.gist: Before all of humanity the Prophet will prostrate beneath the Throne, and Allah will tell him to raise his head; no one else has been told in sujud that it is enough.

outline.heading: Only Allah makes the call that you have done enough
outline.gist: Deciding for ourselves that we have done enough takes from Allah what is His. He makes that call for Muhammad in this life and on the Day of Judgment: ask and you will be given, intercede and it will be accepted.

outline.heading: Bosworth Smith: Caesar and pope in one
outline.gist: He was head of state and of religion without the pope's pretensions or Caesar's legions, bodyguard, palace or revenue; if anyone ruled by divine right it was Muhammad, and his private simplicity matched his public life.

outline.heading: His dua for Aisha, made for his ummah every night
outline.gist: With his head in her lap he asked Allah to forgive all her past and future, open and hidden sins, and she laughed with joy. He told her this is the dua he makes for his ummah every day and night.

outline.heading: His greatness is in his humanity
outline.gist: Allah has none of the weaknesses of the human condition. The Prophet's genius is that he had them, urges, difficulties and challenges, yet carried himself with grace, smiled every day and served his people with compassion.

outline.heading: A simplicity impossible to emulate
outline.gist: With all he had access to he lived so simply that he seemed untempted by wealth or luxury, so that people sometimes forget he was human. Send more salawat on him, especially on a Friday that is also the day of his birth.

outline.heading: Michael Hart ranks him first
outline.gist: His life was the miracle: he achieved the outcomes. Hart, ranking influence rather than goodness, put him first because he was born into no royalty or wealth, in an ignored and backward part of the world.

outline.heading: He sealed his own legacy
outline.gist: Unlike prophets whose followers wrote their legacy, he secured his own: religious unity for Arabia and political leadership of a nation, which continued after his death. Most Muslims today are Muslim because of what came after him, because he invested in people.

outline.heading: A thousand leaders, not buildings
outline.gist: His life shows no meetings about buildings or fundraising, only educating and empowering people; he left a thousand men each capable of leading a nation. Medina when he died had a small masjid.

outline.heading: The people were the legacy: invest in hearts
outline.gist: The masjid had no roof and his homes had ceilings you could touch; an assessor would see nothing impressive but the people. Invest in hearts, minds and souls to bring back his legacy of functional households and communities, and celebrate him by understanding who he was.

outline.heading: Interlude
Sounding the alarm: no defined communal goals
outline.gist: He brings back the communal objectives he presented about three years ago, which still stand. Speaking as a teacher in the masjid, he says the community does not know where it is going: projects happen because three people with influence agree, whether needed or not.

outline.heading: Nothing to hold anyone to; first, education
outline.gist: Without defined goals no one can be held to anything, and coming every Friday has no endgame. The first objective is an educated community that knows its deen, ethics, principles and values.

outline.heading: Mentorship: hand the baton down
outline.gist: Education must be academic and professional too. A gap between the outgoing and incoming generations means the community is failing, so youth must connect with the middle-aged and the middle-aged with elders.

outline.heading: Outreach to Muslims and non-Muslims
outline.gist: The Prophet's life was dawah. Thousands of Muslims, many our own relatives, do not pray or raise their children well; and non-Muslims, if they took this deen, would do better with it than we do.

outline.heading: Centralizing finances through zakat
outline.gist: He is ashamed to have the perfect role model and do nothing with it. Financial centralization is the one form he thinks possible: pooled zakat could fund what matters and care for the weak, our own and others.

outline.heading: Advocacy, after 700 days
outline.gist: He knows of no precedent in history for 700 days of a people bombarded and systematically killed with no army on the other side, only children, journalists and doctors. We must define our goals and hold ourselves accountable.

outline.heading: Love him by standing for his ummah
outline.gist: He wept at night for his ummah, and when Jibril asked why, Allah promised he would be pleased with it on the Day of Judgment. Whether that holds in this life is up to us.

outline.heading: Outro

q7gLFqITcBE.title: Subbuhun Quddus: Glorifying Allah in Ruku and Sujud
q7gLFqITcBE.one_line: A short reminder on the dhikr 'Subbuhun Quddus, Rabb al-mala'ikah wa al-ruh' and how to say the adhkar of prayer with presence.
q7gLFqITcBE.summary: A brief hadith-of-the-week reminder continuing a series on the adhkar of ruku and sujud. The speaker presents the narration in Muslim, Abu Dawud and Ahmad that the Prophet would say in bowing and prostration that Allah is glorified and most holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit. He recalls that ruku centres on glorifying Allah, standing after it on praise, and sujud on dua, and that the Prophet varied his words to keep the heart engaged. He explains subbuh as declaring Allah free of every flaw, including the claim of a child and the partners people worship, and the Spirit as Jibril, the angel of revelation. If the pure angels never tire of glorifying Allah, we should be humbler still. He asks listeners to add this dhikr to the ones covered earlier, recite slowly, and focus on one formula per prayer or rak'ah so the heart can dwell on its meaning.

outline.heading: Meaning of subbuh, quddus and al-ruh
outline.gist: Allah is free of every imperfection; the Spirit is Jibril; the angels glorify Him without ceasing, so we should be humbler still.

outline.heading: Living one dhikr per prayer
outline.gist: Recite slowly, feel you stand before the King, and assign one formula to a prayer or rak'ah to keep the mind focused.

30:41.ar: ظَهَرَ ٱلۡفَسَادُ فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتۡ أَيۡدِي ٱلنَّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهُم بَعۡضَ ٱلَّذِي عَمِلُواْ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
30:41.en: Corruption doth appear on land and sea because of (the evil) which men's hands have done, that He may make them taste a part of that which they have done, in order that they may return

30:42.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلُۚ كَانَ أَكۡثَرُهُم مُّشۡرِكِينَ
30:42.en: Say (O Muhammad, to the disbelievers): Travel in the land, and see the nature of the consequence for those who were before you! Most of them were idolaters

30:43.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ ٱلۡقَيِّمِ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ يَوۡمࣱ لَّا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۖ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَصَّدَّعُونَ
30:43.en: So set thy purpose resolutely for the right religion, before the inevitable day cometh from Allah. On that day mankind will be sundered

30:44.ar: مَن كَفَرَ فَعَلَيۡهِ كُفۡرُهُۥۖ وَمَنۡ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَلِأَنفُسِهِمۡ يَمۡهَدُونَ
30:44.en: Whoso disbelieveth must (then) bear the consequences of his disbelief, while those who do right make provision for themselves

30:45.ar: لِيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
30:45.en: That He may reward out of His bounty those who believe and do good works. Lo! He loveth not the disbelievers (in His guidance)

30:46.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَن يُرۡسِلَ ٱلرِّيَاحَ مُبَشِّرَٰتࣲ وَلِيُذِيقَكُم مِّن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ وَلِتَجۡرِيَ ٱلۡفُلۡكُ بِأَمۡرِهِۦ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
30:46.en: And of His signs is this: He sendeth herald winds to make you taste His mercy, and that the ships may sail at His command, and that ye may seek his favour, and that haply ye may be thankful

30:47.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ رُسُلًا إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِمۡ فَجَآءُوهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ فَٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَجۡرَمُواْۖ وَكَانَ حَقًّا عَلَيۡنَا نَصۡرُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
30:47.en: Verily We sent before thee (Muhammad) messengers to their own folk. Then we took vengeance upon those who were guilty (in regard to them). To help believers is ever incumbent upon Us

30:48.ar: ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي يُرۡسِلُ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابࣰ ا فَيَبۡسُطُهُۥ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ كَيۡفَ يَشَآءُ وَيَجۡعَلُهُۥ كِسَفࣰ ا فَتَرَى ٱلۡوَدۡقَ يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡ خِلَٰلِهِۦۖ فَإِذَآ أَصَابَ بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦٓ إِذَا هُمۡ يَسۡتَبۡشِرُونَ
30:48.en: Allah is He Who sendeth the winds so that they raise clouds, and spreadeth them along the sky as pleaseth Him, and causeth them to break and thou seest the rain downpouring from within them. And when He maketh it to fall on whom He will of His bondmen, lo! they rejoice

30:49.ar: وَإِن كَانُواْ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيۡهِم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمُبۡلِسِينَ
30:49.en: Though before that, even before it was sent down upon them, they were in despair

30:50.ar: فَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِ رَحۡمَتِ ٱللَّهِ كَيۡفَ يُحۡيِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَآۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
30:50.en: Look, therefore, at the prints of Allah's mercy (in creation): how He quickeneth the earth after her death. Lo! He verily is the Quickener of the Dead, and He is Able to do all things

30:51.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا رِيحࣰ ا فَرَأَوۡهُ مُصۡفَرࣰّ ا لَّظَلُّواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ يَكۡفُرُونَ
30:51.en: And if We sent a wind and they beheld it yellow, they verily would still continue in their disbelief

30:52.ar: فَإِنَّكَ لَا تُسۡمِعُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَلَا تُسۡمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوۡاْ مُدۡبِرِينَ
30:52.en: For verily thou (Muhammad) canst not make the dead to hear, nor canst thou make the deaf to hear the call when they have turned to flee

30:53.ar: وَمَآ أَنتَ بِهَٰدِ ٱلۡعُمۡيِ عَن ضَلَٰلَتِهِمۡۖ إِن تُسۡمِعُ إِلَّا مَن يُؤۡمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ
30:53.en: Nor canst thou guide the blind out of their error. Thou canst make none to hear save those who believe in Our revelations so that they surrender (unto Him)

30:3.ar: فِيٓ أَدۡنَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ غَلَبِهِمۡ سَيَغۡلِبُونَ
30:3.en: In the nearer land, and they, after their defeat will be victorious

30:4.ar: فِي بِضۡعِ سِنِينَۗ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ مِن قَبۡلُ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدُۚ وَيَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَفۡرَحُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
30:4.en: Within ten years - Allah's is the command in the former case and in the latter - and in that day believers will rejoice

30:31.ar: ۞مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيۡهِ وَٱتَّقُوهُ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَلَا تَكُونُواْ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ
30:31.en: Turning unto Him (only); and be careful of your duty unto Him and establish worship, and be not of those who ascribe partners (unto Him)

30:32.ar: مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمۡ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعࣰ اۖ كُلُّ حِزۡبِۭ بِمَا لَدَيۡهِمۡ فَرِحُونَ
30:32.en: Of those who split up their religion and became schismatics, each sect exulting in its tenets

30:28.ar: ضَرَبَ لَكُم مَّثَلࣰ ا مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡۖ هَل لَّكُم مِّن مَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُم مِّن شُرَكَآءَ فِي مَا رَزَقۡنَٰكُمۡ فَأَنتُمۡ فِيهِ سَوَآءࣱ تَخَافُونَهُمۡ كَخِيفَتِكُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لِقَوۡمࣲ يَعۡقِلُونَ
30:28.en: He coineth for you a similitude of yourselves. Have ye, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in the wealth We have bestowed upon you, equal with you in respect thereof, so that ye fear them as ye fear each other (that ye ascribe unto Us partners out of that which We created)? Thus We display the revelations for people who have sense

30:30.ar: فَأَقِمۡ وَجۡهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفࣰ اۚ فِطۡرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِي فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيۡهَاۚ لَا تَبۡدِيلَ لِخَلۡقِ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلۡقَيِّمُ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:30.en: So set thy purpose (O Muhammad) for religion as a man by nature upright - the nature (framed) of Allah, in which He hath created man. There is no altering (the laws of) Allah's creation. That is the right religion, but most men know not

17:7.ar: إِنۡ أَحۡسَنتُمۡ أَحۡسَنتُمۡ لِأَنفُسِكُمۡۖ وَإِنۡ أَسَأۡتُمۡ فَلَهَاۚ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعۡدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لِيَسُـُٔواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ وَلِيَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَلِيُتَبِّرُواْ مَا عَلَوۡاْ تَتۡبِيرًا
17:7.en: (Saying): If ye do good, ye do good for your own souls, and if ye do evil, it is for them (in like manner). So, when the time for the second (of the judgments) came (We roused against you others of Our slaves) to ravage you, and to enter the Temple even as they entered it the first time, and to lay waste all that they conquered with an utter wasting

104:2.en: Who hath gathered wealth (of this world) and arranged it

104:3.en: He thinketh that his wealth will render him immortal

104:4.en: Nay, but verily he will be flung to the Consuming One

104:5.en: Ah, what will convey unto thee what the Consuming One is

MZZkfPkqX2k.speaker: adnan
MZZkfPkqX2k.speaker_note: his Friday Arabic tafsir; continues his Ar-Rum series from the previous week in his own voice
MZZkfPkqX2k.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surah Ar-Rum (30:41-50)
MZZkfPkqX2k.one_line: Ar-Rum's laws of Allah: corruption spreads and returns to its doer, reward is pure grace, life runs on motion and work, and every deed leaves traces.
MZZkfPkqX2k.summary: He reads this passage of Ar-Rum as a set of divine laws. Corruption appearing on land and sea is a self-correcting system: harm spreads and comes back to its doer so people return, and he warns that any family or company that rewards the lazy and loads the diligent will collapse. Things are judged by their outcomes, so every prohibition leads to harm and every command to good. Shirk in this surah's context means following laws other than Allah's, such as the jungle rule that the strong deserve whatever they take. Setting one's face to the upright religion means devoting oneself wholly to its values. He offers his own reading of people cracking apart on the Last Day: corruption is a crack that travels outward and returns to the one who made it, like a ripple effect, which makes careless words and mockery dangerous. Reward in paradise comes from Allah's bounty, since we owe Him a debt we can never repay. The winds and ships show a law of continuous motion; he contrasts this with idleness and cafe culture in Muslim lands and with the emigrants who went straight to work in Madinah. He ends on looking at the traces of mercy and judging our own deeds, from prayer to family visits, by the effects they leave.

outline.heading: Opening
Corruption on land and sea: a self-correcting system
outline.gist: Harm never stops at the act; it spreads and returns to its doer. If wrongdoing made life better nothing would stop it, so Allah built in a law that pushes people back toward good.

outline.heading: Never reward the corrupt and punish the diligent
outline.gist: An aside on upbringing and management: giving the hard worker more work at the same pay while the lazy coast ruins any company or system.

outline.heading: Judge things by their outcomes
outline.gist: Extravagance, oppression, lies, haram money and zina feel good in the moment but end badly, as overeating does; every command leads to good and every prohibition to corruption.

outline.heading: Travel and see the end of those before
outline.gist: People are invited to verify this law by looking at what happened to arrogant nations and individuals; most of them were mushrikin.

outline.heading: Shirk in this surah: following other laws
outline.gist: Words like shirk take their meaning from each surah's context; here it means believing someone other than Allah sets the laws, like the jungle rule that the strong deserve what they grab.

outline.heading: Set your face to the upright religion
outline.gist: The surah gives the command twice, once for the religion of fitrah and once for the religion full of values; setting your face means devoting your whole self to it before a day no one can avert.

outline.heading: On that day they crack apart
outline.gist: Yassadda'un is a rare word meaning to split; the common reading is that people crack from the awe of the Day.

outline.heading: The crack you start comes back to you
outline.gist: His own reading: corruption is a crack that travels outward like a ripple or butterfly effect and on the Last Day returns to split the one who caused it.

outline.heading: Whoever disbelieves bears it; the righteous pave their own road
outline.gist: Good deeds smooth the road to paradise, which is lined with hardships; some will cross the Sirat in a blink and others will spend longer on it than they lived.

outline.heading: A careless word can drop you seventy years
outline.gist: Our choices affect others and their consequences return to us, so increase repentance and good deeds since you never know a word's effect.

outline.heading: If mockery earns Al-Humazah, what of those who kill?
outline.gist: A wink or a sneer can damage someone's life; if the Quran warns slanderers of the crushing fire, imagine those who imprison, starve and kill people.

outline.heading: Everyone receives the traces of their deeds
outline.gist: Disbelief and good deeds both come back to their owner; he flags athar, traces, as the word to watch in this page.

outline.heading: Reward from His bounty, not by fair price
outline.gist: No deed could pay for life, senses or provision; we owe Allah a debt we can never repay, so the relationship is one of love and grace, not a job with a boss.

outline.heading: He does not love the disbelievers
outline.gist: Citing Ibn Ashur, he says being told Allah does not love them is a punishment harder on their souls than hell itself.

outline.heading: Reading 30:46-47 and the three ra's
outline.gist: He recites the next verses and points out which ra is heavy and which is light in the phrase about the winds bearing good news.

outline.heading: The law of continuous motion
outline.gist: Winds bring rain, ships sail and people seek Allah's bounty together; life depends on this constant movement, and its purpose is gratitude.

outline.heading: Stagnation and cafe culture in Muslim lands
outline.gist: In a country where he stayed for months, people sleep at dawn, open shops late and fill cafes every night with no work; such stagnation ruins whole nations.

outline.heading: The emigrants went straight to work
outline.gist: The Makkan emigrants became traders in Madinah, and about seventy Qurra taught the Ahl al-Suffah and new arrivals Quran and a trade so they could earn.

outline.heading: All the prophets' stories in one verse; victory is a right Allah set on Himself
outline.gist: Messengers came with proofs, criminals were punished, and helping the believers who respect all of Allah's laws is a right Allah made binding on Himself.

outline.heading: Idleness of thought
outline.gist: Unemployment is not only about money; if you have no job, seek knowledge or learn a trade, since no one in history was handed a living while sitting at home.

outline.heading: Another example of mishandling Allah's laws
outline.gist: As earlier in the surah with people who call on Allah only in harm, verses 48 to 53 give a further example, to be continued next week.

outline.heading: Interlude
Winds that raise clouds
outline.gist: The Arabs named every wind and read its clouds: cold winds and dark clouds meant rain, yellow clouds meant sand and ruined crops.

outline.heading: Clouds in fragments and heavy rain bursting through
outline.gist: Allah spreads clouds as He wills or breaks them into pieces, and wadq is heavy, large-drop rain; those it reaches rejoice at the good season ahead.

outline.heading: Before it they were in despair
outline.gist: Iblas is complete loss of hope, which some link to the name Iblis; the repeated 'before' points to their despair before they even saw the winds and clouds.

outline.heading: Look at the traces of Allah's mercy
outline.gist: He revives dead land literally and revives despairing hearts figuratively, turning despair into glad tidings.

outline.heading: Every act has traces beyond itself
outline.gist: A prayer discharges an obligation but should also leave light and change; every sin leaves darkness and spreading harm. Ar-Rum's distinct theme is Allah's laws.

outline.heading: The laws govern every nation, Muslim or not
outline.gist: The Romans' defeat and victory showed the laws bind superpowers too; a just nation stands even if disbelieving and an unjust one falls even if Muslim.

outline.heading: Reviving dead land and despairing hearts
outline.gist: Good released from you lands well and leaves a good trace; harm leaves harm, as the destroyed nations show.

outline.heading: Judge your own deeds by their effects
outline.gist: Ask what memorizing Quran, attending a lesson or a family visit actually changed; a gathering spent backbiting relatives left only sins, so change the approach.

outline.heading: He who revives the earth revives the dead
outline.gist: The same power that brings green out of barren land will bring you out of your grave.

outline.heading: Outro

SLdJ5c9F-8I.title: Setting Your Children Up for School Success
SLdJ5c9F-8I.one_line: A pediatric occupational therapist and a teacher give parents back-to-school strategies: sleep, nutrition, play, routines, emotions, anxiety, independence and connection.
SLdJ5c9F-8I.summary: Ten days before school starts, a pediatric occupational therapist and a high school teacher offer parents a framework rather than a checklist: aim for the ideal with realistic, compassionate expectations, understand a behaviour before intervening, and remember that most families parent without a village. They define success as learning, social growth, emotional regulation and confidence, not just grades, and list why school is hard: learning and sensory difficulties, sensitivity, anxiety, lack of belonging, neurodivergence, bullying and home stress, with executive function not mature until the mid-twenties. They then cover the basics: shifting bedtimes back gradually, nine to eleven hours of sleep, checking for mouth breathing, protein breakfasts and fewer sugary drinks, unstructured play, predictable routines, fewer extracurriculars, and screens placed after homework and away from bedtime. On emotions they teach that all feelings are allowed but not all behaviours, use prayer as a daily pause, renew intentions and a growth mindset, smooth mornings by preparing the night before, avoid sibling comparisons, explain anxiety's purpose, and picture a frustration cup. They close with contacting teachers early, caring for the caregiver, after-school restraint collapse, daily connection and repair, the Prophet's attentiveness, and making dua for children.

outline.heading: Framework: ideal parenting with realistic expectations
outline.gist: Self-compassion, understand before you intervene, and parenting without a village while still growing up ourselves.

outline.heading: What success means and why school can be hard
outline.gist: Learning, social and emotional growth over grades; sensory, anxiety, belonging, bullying, home stress, learning styles and immature executive function.

outline.heading: Sleep: the glue that holds us together
outline.gist: Shift bedtimes back gradually, nine to eleven hours for school-age children, no screens before bed, and check snoring or mouth breathing.

outline.heading: Nutrition and play
outline.gist: Protein breakfasts, water over sugary drinks, crunchy snacks, gut health, and daily unstructured play to process the day.

outline.heading: Routines, extracurriculars and screens
outline.gist: Predictable routines free the brain; audit an overloaded week; screens after homework because of their dopamine pull.

outline.heading: Emotions, prayer, intention and growth mindset
outline.gist: All feelings are okay but not all behaviours; prayer as a pause; renew the intention for learning; skills are not fixed.

outline.heading: Mornings, independence and the transition back
outline.gist: Prepare the night before, add buffer time, scaffold tasks, review report cards, visit the school, talk about kindness, and never compare siblings.

outline.heading: Anxiety, fear of failure and the frustration cup
outline.gist: Anxiety has a protective purpose; your track record of getting through hard things is 100 percent; let children empty their cup before demands.

outline.heading: Teachers, caregivers, connection and the prophetic model
outline.gist: Contact teachers early, look after yourself, expect after-school collapse, build connection and repair ruptures, follow the Prophet's attentiveness, and make dua for children.

outline.heading: Outro

72:20.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَدۡعُواْ رَبِّي وَلَآ أُشۡرِكُ بِهِۦٓ أَحَدࣰ ا
72:20.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I pray unto Allah only, and ascribe unto Him no partner

72:21.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّي لَآ أَمۡلِكُ لَكُمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا رَشَدࣰ ا
72:21.en: Say: Lo! I control not hurt nor benefit for you

72:22.ar: قُلۡ إِنِّي لَن يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدࣱ وَلَنۡ أَجِدَ مِن دُونِهِۦ مُلۡتَحَدًا
72:22.en: Say: Lo! none can protect me from Allah, nor can I find any refuge beside Him

72:23.ar: إِلَّا بَلَٰغࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِسَٰلَٰتِهِۦۚ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَإِنَّ لَهُۥ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ أَبَدًا
72:23.en: (Mine is) but conveyance (of the Truth) from Allah, and His messages; and whoso disobeyeth Allah and His messenger, lo! his is fire of hell, wherein such dwell for ever

72:24.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا رَأَوۡاْ مَا يُوعَدُونَ فَسَيَعۡلَمُونَ مَنۡ أَضۡعَفُ نَاصِرࣰ ا وَأَقَلُّ عَدَدࣰ ا
72:24.en: Till (the day) when they shall behold that which they are promised (they may doubt); but then they will know (for certain) who is weaker in allies and less in multitude

72:25.ar: قُلۡ إِنۡ أَدۡرِيٓ أَقَرِيبࣱ مَّا تُوعَدُونَ أَمۡ يَجۡعَلُ لَهُۥ رَبِّيٓ أَمَدًا
72:25.en: Say (O Muhammad, unto the disbelievers): I know not whether that which ye are promised is nigh, or if my Lord hath set a distant term for it

72:26.ar: عَٰلِمُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ فَلَا يُظۡهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيۡبِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا
72:26.en: (He is) the Knower of the Unseen, and He revealeth unto none His secret

72:27.ar: إِلَّا مَنِ ٱرۡتَضَىٰ مِن رَّسُولࣲ فَإِنَّهُۥ يَسۡلُكُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِ يَدَيۡهِ وَمِنۡ خَلۡفِهِۦ رَصَدࣰ ا
72:27.en: Save unto every messenger whom He hath chosen, and then He maketh a guard to go before him and a guard behind him

72:28.ar: لِّيَعۡلَمَ أَن قَدۡ أَبۡلَغُواْ رِسَٰلَٰتِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَحَاطَ بِمَا لَدَيۡهِمۡ وَأَحۡصَىٰ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ عَدَدَۢا
72:28.en: That He may know that they have indeed conveyed the messages of their Lord. He surroundeth all their doings, and He keepeth count of all things

110:2.ar: وَرَأَيۡتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدۡخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفۡوَاجࣰ ا
110:2.en: And thou seest mankind entering the religion of Allah in troops

28:56.ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
28:56.en: Lo! thou (O Muhammad) guidest not whom thou lovest, but Allah guideth whom He will. And He is Best Aware of those who walk aright

71:5.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوۡتُ قَوۡمِي لَيۡلࣰ ا وَنَهَارࣰ ا
71:5.en: He said: My Lord! Lo! I have called unto my people night and day

71:6.ar: فَلَمۡ يَزِدۡهُمۡ دُعَآءِيٓ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
71:6.en: But all my calling doth but add to their repugnance

71:7.ar: وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوۡتُهُمۡ لِتَغۡفِرَ لَهُمۡ جَعَلُوٓاْ أَصَٰبِعَهُمۡ فِيٓ ءَاذَانِهِمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡشَوۡاْ ثِيَابَهُمۡ وَأَصَرُّواْ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ ٱسۡتِكۡبَارࣰ ا
71:7.en: And lo! whenever I call unto them that Thou mayst pardon them they thrust their fingers in their ears and cover themselves with their garments and persist (in their refusal) and magnify themselves in pride

71:8.en: And lo! I have called unto them aloud

71:9.ar: ثُمَّ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَنتُ لَهُمۡ وَأَسۡرَرۡتُ لَهُمۡ إِسۡرَارࣰ ا

LuCtYX7s-Mc.title: Surat Al-Jinn Part 4: Verses 22-28
LuCtYX7s-Mc.one_line: The closing verses of Al-Jinn as four foundations of dawah: tawhid, owning nothing, doing it for oneself, and claiming no hidden knowledge.
LuCtYX7s-Mc.summary: He closes Surat Al-Jinn by reading its final commands to the Prophet as the four foundations of sound dawah. He first sets the frame: Nuh and the Prophet called people in opposite ways with opposite results, which shows that the caller is not judged by the outcome. He then corrects a common misreading of that idea. Not being responsible for results does not license token effort; you are fully responsible for a complete, well-planned effort aimed at people truly finding Allah, and even Nuh and the Prophet expected to account for their work. The four foundations follow: dawah rests on tawhid, not on Islam's practical benefits; the caller owns nothing and has no special status or powers; he conveys the message to save himself, so guidance is given free with no strings attached, while listeners owe Allah and the community, not the teacher; and he claims no knowledge of the unseen beyond what Allah revealed. He calls these verses a safeguard against cult-building, warns against people who claim dreams and secret insight, and shows how breaking each foundation injures dawah. He asks the audience to define the outcome, give full effort, serve the community, and say I don't know when they don't.

outline.heading: Nuh and the jinn: two opposite models of dawah
outline.gist: Nuh preached openly for centuries with few followers; the Prophet did not even know the jinn were listening, yet a whole race accepted. Different methods and outcomes teach that the caller only does his best.

outline.heading: The outcome still defines the effort
outline.gist: Being freed from worry about results does not remove the goal: Muslim victory is people entering the deen and knowing Allah, and every effort must be measured against that.

outline.heading: Misreading 'not responsible for the outcome'
outline.gist: People hear the phrase as permission for a token effort. He asks whether they exhausted every resource, planned, and understood their audience.

outline.heading: Nuh must argue his effort before Allah
outline.gist: The point of Surat Nuh is Nuh explaining to Allah everything he did to reach his people, so the caller is fully responsible for the full effort.

outline.heading: Effort pointed in the wrong direction
outline.gist: If the real aim is recognition, followers or ticking a box, the failure is yours. Muslims have not even defined the outcomes they seek, with their youth or their world.

outline.heading: Foundation one: dawah built on tawhid
outline.gist: Dawah must rest on knowing Allah alone, the constant source of fixed values, not on arguments about Islam's practical benefits, which are results rather than the basis.

outline.heading: Foundation two: the caller owns nothing
outline.gist: No one has special powers, healing or a seat at a table with God. A good speaker must refuse the status people try to give him.

outline.heading: Even the mightiest prophets account for their work
outline.gist: Nuh is the first of the five great messengers and still argues his case; the Prophet at the farewell sermon asked people to testify that he conveyed. Muslims who have not even defined the goal should not feel so secure.

outline.heading: Recap and reading of verses 22-24
outline.gist: We cannot forgive sins or fix lives; we only offer guidance as it was gifted to us. He introduces the third foundation, which runs over three verses.

outline.heading: Foundation three: conveying the message to save oneself
outline.gist: He teaches for his own protection and listeners attend for theirs. Guidance, unlike food or care from parents, must come with no strings attached.

outline.heading: Prophets ask for no reward
outline.gist: Every prophet's refrain that they ask for no payment, and the Quran's question whether the Prophet asks a fee that weighs people down, show guidance must be free.

outline.heading: No refuge from Allah except conveying
outline.gist: Multahad means a protective barrier, as the lahd of the grave; the only barrier between him and Allah's punishment is delivering the message.

outline.heading: The disobedient and the promised day
outline.gist: He restates the foundations: a simple pure message, no special powers, and no favour owed either way.

outline.heading: Knowing what is owed lets love grow
outline.gist: When the minimum is clear, anything extra becomes kindness. Listeners owe Allah and the community, not the teacher, and each must find his part.

outline.heading: Who truly has fewer helpers
outline.gist: People who feel strong and self-sufficient see no need to listen. On the Day they will see who was weaker and outnumbered.

outline.heading: Coming to the masjid only when in need
outline.gist: Wealthy families who appear only for funerals or board elections treat the deen as a service; they will learn whether they needed it.

outline.heading: Expectations and entitlement in marriage
outline.gist: Marriages fail through unhealthy expectations. When each spouse knows the clear minimum, everything beyond it is received as love rather than demanded.

outline.heading: Every masjid program is dawah
outline.gist: The obligation is shared. Classes, Quran programs, mentorship, outreach, even tutoring and social clubs exist to bring people closer to Allah, or they should be removed.

outline.heading: Tajweed of man-irtada
outline.gist: The kasra on the noon only breaks two sukuns, so the following ra stays heavy; moving gracefully between heavy and light letters is most of the skill.

outline.heading: Foundation four: I do not know when it comes
outline.gist: The Prophet does not know whether the promise is near or far. He recaps all four foundations.

outline.heading: The unseen revealed only to chosen messengers
outline.gist: Allah gives access to the unseen only to a messenger he approves, guarded in front and behind so the knowledge does not leak out.

outline.heading: Verses that prevent cult-building
outline.gist: The four foundations remove the preacher from the story. True friends of Allah never broadcast their dreams; those who do are lying.

outline.heading: Never claim knowledge you lack
outline.gist: Most harm in dawah, at home or with non-Muslims, comes from answering what you do not know. Being comfortable with not knowing is half of knowledge.

outline.heading: How breaking each foundation injures dawah
outline.gist: Basing dawah on a figure, granting someone special status, acting as a favour, attaching strings, or disrespecting classical sources all damage it; a faith rests on Allah's guidance, not on the teacher.

outline.heading: Allah encompasses and counts every step
outline.gist: The surah ends by reminding that Allah establishes whether His servants conveyed properly and has counted all they did.

outline.heading: Outro

WBvEhxkeDDg.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Goals and Accountability (Part 2)
WBvEhxkeDDg.one_line: 'I tried my best' needs an object: Allah promised stewardship, an established deen and security, and the ummah lacks all three.
WBvEhxkeDDg.summary: He closes the 'Achieving the Outcomes' series with its sharpest point. Muslims rightly say Allah judges effort, not results, but he hears the phrase misused to avoid asking whether the goal was reached or even what it was. 'I tried my best' is an incomplete sentence; it needs the object Allah set, just as a father's effort is meaningless unless the family agrees on his job. He is certain that Muslims today, as individuals, institutions and an ummah, do not know what they are trying to achieve. Surah An-Nur then supplies one of the Quran's few explicit worldly promises: stewardship and autonomy, an established deen, and security in place of fear, the three pillars of any civilization. Muslims have none of them, so either the promise is doubted or the conditions have not been met. The Prophet's three requests show where the fault lies: Allah granted that the ummah would never be wiped out by divine punishment or destroyed by an external enemy, but refused to prevent internal destruction. The ummah's fate is therefore entirely in its own hands. Mosques must define their outcomes: a boy who recites beautifully but litters, lies and cannot be trusted is a failure of teaching. Every negative trait the Quran names comes with an alternative, and those alternatives are the outcomes; the companions, he recalls, learned eman before Quran.

outline.heading: Opening
An-Nur 24:54: each side carries its own burden
outline.gist: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger; whoever turns away carries the burden he chose, and whoever follows him finds guidance. The Messenger is only responsible for making the message clear.

outline.heading: Misusing 'we are only responsible for effort'
outline.gist: The phrase is correct, but it is often used to avoid asking whether the outcome was achieved and to shed responsibility for the goal.

outline.heading: Complete the sentence: your best toward what?
outline.gist: Allah will only hold you to the best you could do, but is your best aimed at the goal He set? 'I tried my best' needs its object, not 'to finish Super Mario Brothers', before Allah can say 'yes, My servant, I accept it'.

outline.heading: A family must agree on the goals
outline.gist: Effort toward goals Allah does not prioritize may not be excused. A father's best means nothing unless the family agrees on his job, and children who think their goal is staying up late or finishing video games are not on the same page; we must be on the same page with Allah.

outline.heading: Individuals, institutions and the ummah are lost
outline.gist: Young Muslims who bring him their problems do not know what they are here to do, nor do leaders, institutions and organizations, and the ummah is completely lost. Our best now has to go into working out what we are here to achieve.

outline.heading: An-Nur 24:55: one of the few explicit worldly promises
outline.gist: Back to the verse he opened with, and the one Allah adds after it. The Quran is full of promises of reward, but very few state a worldly outcome with no other reading; this is one, for those who believe and let their eman dictate their deeds.

outline.heading: Stewardship, autonomy and an established deen
outline.gist: First, they will be made stewards of the earth with control over their own destiny and decisions, as believers before them were. Second, Allah will establish for them the deen He is pleased with.

outline.heading: Security after fear; then prayer, zakat and obedience
outline.gist: Third, the fear they lived with will be replaced by safety, as long as they keep obeying. Then: establish prayer, give zakat, obey the Messenger, and do not think your enemies are beyond Allah's reach.

outline.heading: We have none of the three
outline.gist: Muslims control neither their destiny nor their decisions, the deen is not properly established even in Muslim countries, and Muslims are secure nowhere. Do you question His promise, or what we had to do to receive it?

outline.heading: The three pillars of any civilization
outline.gist: Many have stopped coming to Jumuah and lost hope; those who come still trust the promise. Stewardship, an established deen and safety are the pillars without which no community, society or nation exists, so why do we not have them?

outline.heading: An unusually long prayer
outline.gist: The companions knew exactly how long his prayers took, and one night he prayed far longer than usual. When they asked, he said it was a prayer full of hope and fear.

outline.heading: First request: no punishment that wipes the ummah out
outline.gist: He asked that his ummah not be destroyed by a general punishment like earlier nations, and it was granted. Nobody says alhamdulillah for this; we feel entitled to a gift he begged for so that we would have time to repent.

outline.heading: Second request: no external enemy can destroy it
outline.gist: He asked that no foreign power be able to overpower and wipe out the ummah, and that was granted too.

outline.heading: Third request refused: they will destroy one another
outline.gist: He asked that they not fight among themselves, and was told no: they will kill and enslave one another and do the harm others cannot. These texts are meant to empower, not depress.

outline.heading: Our destiny is in our hands
outline.gist: Allah gives time to repent and no nation can destroy us, so our reality and future are ours to decide: go and bring back those who stopped coming. If we succeed it is us, if we fail it is us.

outline.heading: What is teaching Quran and prayer meant to produce?
outline.gist: He cannot define outcomes for every field, only for the masjid. Children must learn to read Quran and pray, but those acts are meant to achieve something, or they go and pray in a park and leave their garbage behind.

outline.heading: Recites beautifully but cannot be trusted
outline.gist: A boy taught Quran but not to lower his gaze, respect women and his wife, keep family ties, eat only halal and never cheat or lie has a beautiful voice and no trust. No parent would accept that outcome.

outline.heading: Install the positive values, strip the negative
outline.gist: Deep down everyone knows there are outcomes to achieve. Religious teaching must help people pick up every positive value and remove every negative one, such as turning to God in hardship and forgetting Him in ease.

outline.heading: Children who can recite but cannot handle life
outline.gist: What is the point of teaching children the deen if they cannot handle hardship and ease, treat people well, carry ambition or learn from their past? He sets out to draw from the Quran what it sees as negative in human behaviour and what it offers instead.

outline.heading: A companion's complaint: eman before Quran
outline.gist: Every negative trait the Quran names comes with an alternative, and those alternatives are the outcomes. A companion who lived into extreme old age said they were taught eman, values and how to carry themselves before Quran, and saw later mosques reversing the order.

outline.heading: Something is wrong in how we operate
outline.gist: Allah promised outcomes we do not have, so if we still believe Him, the question is what we must do differently.

outline.heading: Interlude
Al-Ankabut 29:45: is our prayer working?
outline.gist: Knowing the Quran means understanding and practising it. Prayer is meant to keep you from indecency and wrong; if it does not, we must have learned or used it incorrectly.

ZQ59dUp3kpA.one_line: Why inner misalignment keeps us dissatisfied, trauma and blame, not disclosing sins, comfort as the enemy of growth, and keeping roles in priority.
ZQ59dUp3kpA.summary: The sheikh explains that living in dissatisfaction while chasing moments of joy comes from misalignment between who we are and how we present or behave. Like a strained marriage kept alive only by constant busyness, we avoid ourselves, and admitting we were wrong is half the work. With trauma the pattern reverses: Shaytan makes people blame themselves for what they could not change and excuse what they could, so healing involves accepting it was not one's fault, accepting the decree and getting therapy. Pending issues pile up, so open the closet and deal with them one by one. Answering questions, he says to build love for dhikr by learning its value rather than waiting for feeling, and to never disclose past sins, even to a prospective spouse, though one must not lie. Tazkiyah is by design uncomfortable, since comfort means no growth, and it is a path walked daily, not a destination. Its teachings are for oneself, not to project onto others; step back from company that brings out the worst. The raw self is not a set of values but a consciousness that is a servant of a Creator who needs nothing. Having few roles says nothing about one's iman, but primary roles toward parents, spouse and children come before community work.

outline.heading: Past sins and a future spouse
outline.gist: Do not lie if asked directly, but do not volunteer details; once a secret leaves you it is gone, so seek wise counsel.

outline.heading: Comfort equals no growth

outline.heading: Self-inflicted friction

outline.heading: Wanting to look ascetic

outline.heading: A daily priority

outline.heading: A path, not a destination

outline.heading: Question: sinning around certain people

outline.heading: Step back and choose good company

outline.heading: Two good people who bring out the worst

outline.heading: Question: is the essence a set of values?

outline.heading: Serve with whatever you have
outline.gist: Like planting the sapling as the Hour comes, serve through whatever roles Allah gives you without fixating on results.

outline.heading: Dhikr as the worship of the raw self

outline.heading: Roles in their proper order

B3Rsxig893Y.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Striving to Change
B3Rsxig893Y.one_line: Mujahadah, striving, is the pinnacle of Islam, but it only becomes real change with the right objective, tools, teams and continuity.
B3Rsxig893Y.summary: Episode of 'Achieving the Outcomes' on how striving (jihad, mujahadah) becomes actual change. He opens with a realist's audit: record numbers of Muslims, masajid and scholars, yet the ummah is heading backwards and watches Gaza's children starve daily. Mujahadah, exerting effort, is the pinnacle of Islam, used in the Quran before combat was permitted and broadened by the Prophet to striving against the self, earning for one's family and caring for widows; everyone strives in their own field, and when life is lived for Allah's sake even eating, sleeping and marriage earn reward. So why do millions of striving Muslims produce no change? Four things are missing. First, the right objective: effort poured into unneeded buildings or into money is wasted, the saddest thing he knows, and he doubts that 'I thought it was right' will excuse us when we had the means to find out. As-Saff 61:10-11 makes iman plus striving the transaction with Allah. Second, the right tools, asking whether a year of street protests achieved what political advocacy might have. Third, the right teams: parallel uncoordinated efforts reinvent the wheel. Fourth, continuity: people burn for two or three years and vanish. The Prophet channelled the energy of a resourceless people into lasting change and never slowed down; that relentlessness is the model.

outline.heading: Opening
From striving to actual change
outline.gist: The title is a play on words: the real question is how striving, jihad in Quranic language, turns into change we can see and live. Humanity has advanced in technology, science and medicine and still is not living well.

outline.heading: Record numbers of Muslims and masajid
outline.gist: There have never been more Muslims, a higher percentage of Muslims, or more masajid and universities on earth. These statistics are misleading because they give a false sense that things are going well.

outline.heading: Realism: heading backwards while Gaza starves
outline.gist: This is realism, not pessimism: the graph is still going down. Every major city has a Muslim community with masajid, scholars and youth programs, yet we watch children starve and journalists killed daily, seventy-plus years and almost two years without pause.

outline.heading: Jihad as the pinnacle: exhausting effort
outline.gist: The Prophet called striving the peak of Islam; the root means to exhaust effort toward a cause. The word appears in a Makkan surah when bearing arms was still prohibited, and the Arabs understood it as hard work.

outline.heading: Striving against the self and earning for family
outline.gist: The mujahid strives against his own whims for Allah. When the companions wished an energetic man's work were for Allah, the Prophet said going out to feed himself, his children or his parents is for Allah.

outline.heading: Caring for widows is like striving all day
outline.gist: Whoever looks after widows and the needy is like one in Allah's cause all day, and many authentic hadith say the same. The peak of the deen is ongoing striving in whatever field you are good at.

outline.heading: Each in his own field: striving toward what?
outline.gist: Combat has always been the work of a small percentage; most strive in other ways. But striving without knowing what we are trying to change runs into real difficulty.

outline.heading: A life for Allah makes everything that sustains it rewarded
outline.gist: When life is lived for Allah, eating, sleeping, vacation and marital relations are rewarded, just as a company that sends you on a trip pays for your food and lodging. The Prophet told the puzzled companions that halal relations are rewarded as haram ones would be punished.

outline.heading: Why millions striving bring no change
outline.gist: Millions have dedicated their lives to striving for Allah, so why is there no change? Striving turns into change only when certain things are in place.

outline.heading: First condition: the right objective
outline.gist: Striving for the wrong thing is wasted energy. People work day and night to build masajid, but what if that is not what we need?

outline.heading: Money: real striving toward a dead end
outline.gist: People burn their lives for money and end empty, leaving it to ungrateful heirs waiting to inherit. Watching people strive hard toward a dead end is, for him, the saddest thing in the world.

outline.heading: As-Saff: iman plus striving is the transaction
outline.gist: Allah offers a transaction that saves from punishment: believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive. Forgiveness, Paradise and success are offered in return, and there is no way around this relationship.

outline.heading: Will a wrong objective be excused?
outline.gist: It terrifies him to give a life of effort and deprivation only to learn it was the wrong objective. He doubts that 'I thought it was right' will work when we had the means to find out what was needed.

outline.heading: Convenience: striving for what is flashy
outline.gist: Striving for what we do not need comes from laziness and convenience. Money brings something for us, and buildings are concrete you can point at with your name on a plaque.

outline.heading: The unglamorous needs: mental health, marriages, children
outline.gist: Much of the needed striving, mental health support, marital support and raising children, earns no plaque or recognition and cannot be cashed in. If we want inner and outer change, a few things must be worked out.

outline.heading: Second condition: the right tools
outline.gist: Define what pleases Allah and serves the community, then choose tools that do not waste effort. We stood on the streets and shouted for a year; might a fraction of that money in political advocacy have done more? He admits he has no answers but insists the community can work it out.

outline.heading: Third condition: the right teams
outline.gist: Groups striving toward the same goal in parallel go at half speed, hit the same problems and reinvent the wheel. An ummah built on jama'ah fails to coordinate because people refuse to reach out, ask and work with other groups.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet's mastery of channelling energy
outline.gist: From a resourceless spot in Arabia around the first house of Allah, he harnessed the energy of the people around him and taught them to channel it together toward a helpful objective. After his death they continued through failures and produced one of history's most impressive stories.

outline.heading: Fourth condition: continuity
outline.gist: Momentum must not stop. People commit for two or three years, disappear for as long and come back, as he sees from living in the masjid.

outline.heading: Relentless like the Prophet: stick to the task
outline.gist: The Prophet's relentlessness is seldom discussed: no one could distract him, slow him down or persuade him to take time off. Stick to the task until it is done; without these four elements the ummah cannot turn striving into change.

outline.heading: Outro

y-mTO1k-7IU.title: Intellectual Development and Learning Disorders: Facts and Warning Signs (Part 2)
y-mTO1k-7IU.one_line: Dr. Sohail Makhdoom covers prenatal folate, early warning signs, speech, motor and tic disorders, intellectual disability levels, learning disorders and lifestyle factors.
y-mTO1k-7IU.summary: In a second community health session, Dr. Sohail Makhdoom starts from pregnancy: the nervous system forms before most women know they are pregnant, so women of reproductive age should take folic acid and B12. For young children he advises patience: the first five years are for gathering information, five to eight for adapting the approach, and only after eight to ten should persistent difficulties lead to formal assessment, after ruling out hearing, vision, thyroid and seizures. He describes speech and language disorders, stuttering fed by anxiety, social communication disorder versus autism, developmental coordination disorder, and tics and Tourette's, stressing education of teachers and peers and adjusted expectations. Answering a Quran teacher about a child struggling with Arabic letters, he notes that a third language complicates the picture. He outlines mild, moderate and severe intellectual disability by IQ range and adult functional age, and specific learning disorders such as dyslexia that affect 5 to 15 percent of children, warning that parent and teacher blame harms the child. He ends with nutrition, hydration, exercise, sleep, no screens before bed, and parents' availability and patterns at home as factors in performance.

outline.heading: Prenatal development and folic acid
outline.gist: Major organs form within weeks, so women of reproductive age should already take folate and B12.

outline.heading: Early years: communication, hearing, vision and brain pruning
outline.gist: Look for attempts to communicate; check hearing and vision first; the brain prunes connections based on environment, so avoid early labels.

outline.heading: Challenging behaviours and an age-based approach
outline.gist: Self-harm and biting drive referrals; gather information to five, adapt approach five to eight, assess after eight to ten.

outline.heading: Speech disorders, IQ ranges and a Quran teacher's question
outline.gist: Sign language for those who cannot speak; gifted children also disengage; a child learning Arabic as a third language must be judged against his other languages.

outline.heading: Medical causes, stuttering, autism, coordination and tic disorders
outline.gist: Rule out thyroid and seizures; anxiety worsens stuttering and tics; Tourette's is managed by educating adults and adjusting expectations.

outline.heading: Newcomer children and levels of intellectual disability
outline.gist: Give children new to Canada a fair chance first; mild, moderate and severe ranges and the functional age each reaches.

outline.heading: Specific learning disorders and parent-teacher blame
outline.gist: Dyslexia and written expression; 5 to 15 percent of children; families who can afford services catch problems earlier.

outline.heading: Lifestyle: food, exercise, sleep, screens and home patterns
outline.gist: Processed sugar and dyes affect some children with ADHD; nighttime sleep matters most, no screens an hour before bed, and teachers should track patterns with parents.

outline.heading: Outro

GeCtxSJfM7U.title: Achieving the Outcomes: Appearance to Essence
GeCtxSJfM7U.one_line: Outward Muslim appearance must be matched by inner essence; appearance without essence is what Allah named nifaq, and it is the one unfixable type.
GeCtxSJfM7U.summary: Episode of 'Achieving the Outcomes' on moving from appearance (mazhar) to essence (jawhar), which he calls the individual Muslim's biggest struggle since day one. Allah named appearance without essence nifaq, and every sincere believer fears that word. He frames the stakes generationally: young Muslims crave reason and meaning, and we have been presenting Islam as a miserable life redeemed only by Jannah; they are right to find that illogical, because Islam is meant to make this life better, structured and joyful too. His fear is that if people stop blaming the user and start blaming the system, everything is lost. He grounds the point in the hadith that Allah looks at hearts and deeds rather than bodies or wealth, the story of the man with the exaggeratedly bent neck, and the design of salah, ihram and fasting, each built so that outward form provokes and mirrors an inner state. Al-Munafiqun 63:4 pictures the opposite: impressive bodies and enchanting speech, but propped-up decorated wood. Cleanliness and beauty remain required; the problem is when they are all there is. The second khutbah uses a teacher's four-quadrant grid: good appearance with rotten essence is the only unfixable type, which is why Umar kept asking Hudhayfah whether he was on the list of hypocrites. Keep the appearance and keep working on the essence.

outline.heading: Opening
From appearance to essence, and the name Allah gave its absence
outline.gist: The biggest individual struggle of the ummah since day one is having both appearance and essence. Allah named appearance without essence nifaq and named its people; every sincere Muslim fears falling under that word, so the khutbah cannot avoid it.

outline.heading: Why the ummah needs these discussions now
outline.gist: Beyond the oppressed in the Holy Land and the suboptimal state of Muslims in their countries and in the West, the next generation will stop listening if they do not know where Islam is taking them.

outline.heading: Youth crave reason and meaning
outline.gist: The buy-in to Islam is clear, but without knowing the destination people feel lost. Young people crave logic and a higher meaning; Islam has it, but over the last centuries we lost our way in defining its outcomes.

outline.heading: Misery now, Jannah later: a false picture
outline.gist: We almost present Islam to youth as weakness, persecution and misery rewarded only with Jannah, and they are right that it makes no sense. Allah made it the opposite: following Islam properly brings meaning, structure, beauty and joy here, and then Jannah.

outline.heading: Is the problem the system or the user?
outline.gist: Having lost sight of the outcomes, we compromised. Most people still blame the user; if they start blaming the system, we lose everything, and from where he sits that fear is justified.

outline.heading: Step two, not substitution
outline.gist: We are slowly losing the Prophet's way of life because we cannot define its goals. The appearance must stay and the essence be added; nothing in the series has been a substitution, only the next step.

outline.heading: Allah looks at hearts and deeds
outline.gist: Muslim narrates that Allah does not look at your forms, bodies or wealth but at your hearts and deeds: the intentions, hopes, kindness and empathy inside you and what they produce.

outline.heading: Iman is not upright until the heart is
outline.gist: A servant's iman does not reach its goal until the state of his heart shows on his tongue; the heart has to lead, or at least move together with, everything else.

outline.heading: The man with the bent neck
outline.gist: Seeing a man carrying his head down in exaggerated humility, he told him to raise it: khushu is not in the neck, it is in the heart.

outline.heading: Every teaching built to mirror the heart: why salah moves
outline.gist: Almost every ruling is designed so the appearance reflects the heart and the heart the appearance. We stand, bow, prostrate and sit because each movement carries its own invocation and is meant to provoke a different state.

outline.heading: Each posture, the ihram and the fast mirror an inner state
outline.gist: Prostration is the lowest point and the time to ask for aid, standing is for gratitude, bowing for declaring Allah's otherness. The two white cloths of Hajj mirror the heart, and fasting from food mirrors the soul fasting from distraction.

outline.heading: Al-Munafiqun 63:4: impressive bodies, enchanting words
outline.gist: He translates the verse he opened with: when you see them their bodies impress you, and when they speak you listen, as if they were decorated pieces of wood.

outline.heading: Decorated wood that cannot stand
outline.gist: Arabs decorated pieces of wood to beautify their homes, as pilgrims still glue greenery onto wood today. Allah's image: nice on the outside, lifeless inside, unable to stand without leaning on a wall.

outline.heading: Frightened at every cry: the true enemy
outline.gist: Whenever a mistake is pointed out they panic, knowing they carry no weight; they are the enemy, so beware of them. That does not mean coming to the masjid in dirty clothes.

outline.heading: Appearance still matters: cleanliness is half of iman
outline.gist: Cleanliness of body and clothes is required, wudu, clean and new clothes, perfume. The problem is reducing cleanliness to the body alone.

outline.heading: Allah loves beauty, but not beauty alone
outline.gist: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty, so caring for appearance is not forbidden. But good looks with dishonest transactions, untrustworthy work, no empathy and injustice toward spouse and children are pointless.

outline.heading: Interlude
A teacher's grid of appearance and essence
outline.gist: He lays out in Arabic, as he remembers it, a grid one of his teachers once drew on the board, then switches to English to explain it quadrant by quadrant.

outline.heading: First quadrant: the appearance is a duty too
outline.gist: Appropriate appearance is required: in his village people came to the masjid straight from the stable and left you smelling of cows all night. Hijab and how young men present themselves are part of the deen.

outline.heading: Second quadrant: good appearance, rotten essence
outline.gist: The goal is the Prophet's appearance and essence together. Good outside with rotten inside was named nifaq and placed in the lowest depths of the Fire to scare us from securing the appearance and then getting lazy.

outline.heading: Umar asking Hudhayfah about the list
outline.gist: Hudhayfah held the Prophet's list of hypocrites and never released it, which kept them from seeking office for the first thirty years. Umar asked him every day whether he was named.

outline.heading: Why Umar feared, and the dead weight of the ummah
outline.gist: Umar had the appearance and feared he had not gone far enough in the essence. The second group harms the ummah: they come when there is benefit and vanish when there is a load to carry.

outline.heading: Third quadrant: good heart, untaught appearance
outline.gist: Those with poor appearance but empathetic, loving hearts were simply never taught; teach them how to dress and present themselves and they will soar.

outline.heading: Fourth quadrant: corrupt but reformable; only the second is unfixable
outline.gist: Bad outside and inside is at least honest with himself, and family, community and government together can reform him. The only unfixable type is the second, because he knowingly picks the effortless part that makes him look good.

outline.heading: The charge: I look it, now I must be it
outline.gist: Islam exists to bring islah, but the second type cannot be fixed unless he wants it. Each of us must move from looking it to being it; anyone who concludes 'I can't be it so I'll stop looking it' has misunderstood. Aim to be like the Prophet inside and out.

outline.heading: Outro
